definition.en-US: Everything an app remembers at a given moment, and the screen shows what the state says.

analogy.en-US: Like the scoreboard in a game, which holds the current score until the score changes.

definition.en-US: A small space inside your browser where a website can keep data on your own computer, separate from other websites.

analogy.en-US: Like a locker that the hotel gives each guest, which the guest can use but other guests cannot open.

definition.en-US: A short written description of what an app should do, for an AI assistant or a person to follow.

analogy.en-US: Like the note you give a carpenter before a shelf is built, saying what it holds and how big it should be.

definition.en-US: A list of sentences that each start with I can, where the app is finished when every sentence is true.

analogy.en-US: Like the list you tick off before you leave the house, checking that the keys and the wallet are in your bag.

definition.en-US: A saved version of your project, made with a commit, that you can go back to later.

analogy.en-US: Like a save point in a video game, so you can start again from that spot if the next part goes wrong.

definition.en-US: A second copy of your data, kept somewhere else, so you can restore it if the first copy is lost.

analogy.en-US: Like a photocopy of an important letter, kept in a drawer in case the original is lost.

definition.en-US: A rule that shows only the items that match what you chose, and hides the rest.

analogy.en-US: Like a coffee filter, which holds back the grounds and lets only the coffee through.

definition.en-US: The sum of several numbers, found by adding them all together.

analogy.en-US: Like the bill at a restaurant, which adds up the price of every dish you ordered.
